children: Our Bureau New Delhi: Oil and Natural Gas Corp (ONGC) has struck gas at a deepwater well in the Mahanadi offshore basin off the Odisha coast, the state-run explorer said Monday. ONGC struck gas on September 18 at the MN-DW18-1-H-D well, about 43 km off Konark, at a depth of 1,441-1,452 metres.

The well was drilled to a total depth of 1,623 metres under the country's Samudra Manthan deepwater exploration programme. The well, the first drilled by ONGC in the Mahanadi basin under the current campaign, has been flowing gas with "encouraging flow and reservoir pressure" for the past three days, the company said, adding that the discovery is subject to further appraisal and commercial evaluation.

ONGC said the find, along with other discoveries in the area, could potentially be developed through shared facilities enabled by the Petroleum and Natural Gas Rules, 2025, allowing deepwater resources to be brought into production. The official start of drilling of the well took place on July 25 in the presence of petroleum minister Hardeep Singh Puri.

The discovery adds to ONGC's efforts to step up exploration in India's deepwater areas and expand the country's domestic hydrocarbon resource base. The Samudra Manthan Mission is the government's push to accelerate exploration in the country's deep and ultra-deepwater areas and raise domestic oil and gas output. The programme, with an outlay of 84,000 crore through FY31, provides support for seismic surveys, deepwater drilling and common offshore infrastructure, with the government bearing up to half the drilling cost.

title: ONGC Finds Gas at Deepwater Well Off Odisha Coast
